item.title: Momma bear teaches her cub the fine art of ripping open a truck bed cover in a parking lot
item.description: Viral video captures a mother black bear ripping a truck bed cover wide open while her cub watches and learns how to climb up and join the feast.
item.content:encoded:
If you thought a truck bed cover was going to protect your belongings and/or food from bears, think again. They're not likely to pop open your tailgate using the handle to snoop around.

But, as you can see in the video below, bears can rip the bed cover off with ease. Not only that, hopping up on top of a truck bed cover in a parking lot and ripping it open is a teachable moment they can pass along to their cubs.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

You can't see exactly what momma bear is after, but her cub is definitely taking notes as it figures out how to get onto the bed cover to join her.

It's safe to assume the bear isn't interested in camping gear or tools.

She in all likelihood is sniffing out food the truck owner mistakenly thought would be protected in the bed of the truck by the cover.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK OUTDOORS

Perhaps a picnic basket? Whatever it was the bears caught the scent of, the cover was no match for these two.

There's more knowledge that can be passed along here, aside from the fact that your food is not safe from bears in the bed of your truck under a cover.

CROWD TESTS THEIR LUCK GETTING CLOSE TO WILD BEAR FOR PICTURES AND VIDEO AT MOUNT RAINIER

The Instagram account that shared the viral video recognized that and shared the one rule you need to remember if you encounter a mother bear and her cubs, never get between them.

Also, if you encounter them:

• Stay calm and do not run.

• Give them plenty of space and slowly back away.

• Never approach the cubs — even for a photo.

• Keep dogs leashed and under control.

• Don’t climb a tree; black bears and cubs can climb extremely well.

• If the bear changes behavior because of you, you’re already too close.

• Carry bear spray where bears are present — and keep it accessible, not buried in your backpack.

item.title: Moms for Liberty co-founder warns parents about Ms Rachel’s political activism, ‘Not Mr Rogers’
item.description: Ms. Rachel's 21 million YouTube followers may not realize the children's entertainer has waded into political activism, says Moms for Liberty.
item.content:encoded:
Parents may think they are turning on Ms. Rachel for songs, speech lessons and early learning, but the co-founder of parental rights organization Moms for Liberty says they are increasingly exposing their toddlers to political activism.

"She’s using her leadership role for political activism," Tina Descovich, the co-founder of Moms for Liberty, told Fox News Digital.

Ms. Rachel, whose real name is Rachel Griffin Accurso, has more than 21 million YouTube followers and millions more across Instagram and TikTok. She has become increasingly outspoken on political issues, including the Israel-Gaza war, immigration detention and LGBTQ rights.

MS RACHEL CLAIMS CELEBRITIES SILENT ON GAZA WOULD ‘PROBABLY’ SPEAK IF CHILDREN ‘WERE WHITE’

In December, Ms. Rachel was named as a finalist for StopAntisemitism’s 2025 "Antisemite of the Year" designation after the group accused her of promoting Hamas-aligned messaging in posts about Gaza. Other Jewish organizations have defended or supported her advocacy for Palestinian children.

Descovich said parents turn to Ms. Rachel and expect educational programming that will help their children learn to speak, read and prepare for school.

MS RACHEL DEFENDS HER ACTIVISM BY POINTING TO MISTER ROGERS' POLITICAL LEGACY ON CHILDREN'S TV

"She reaches 21 million viewers a year on YouTube alone, and then her social media channels have, like Instagram, I think has five million, TikTok, 10 million, and she seems to think she can divide her personal views from her influence over toddlers, but parents are tuning in to her messaging because they trust her with their toddlers, and I think her shows should all start with a warning label that says, ‘Warning, this woman has been nominated to be the antisemite of the Year in the United States,’ and they should know that before they put her in front of their toddlers," Descovich said.

Instead, she said, parents may now encounter political messaging involving gender identity, immigration and the Israel-Gaza conflict.

MS RACHEL POSTS SUPPORT FOR HIJAB-WEARING KINDERGARTNERS AFTER TRUMP POST

"Parents turn to her to teach their children potentially to be kind and be a good citizen and love your neighbor," Descovich said. "It would be great if she would teach kids the beginnings of learning to read and concepts so that they can be ready for kindergarten, but infiltrating gender ideology with children as young as two and three and four, that's not something parents are expecting or want to put in front of their kids at such a young age."

In June, Ms. Rachel visited an immigration detention facility in Newark, N.J., called Delaney Hall to be with families she said had been "terrorized" by immigration enforcement.

MS RACHEL DOUBLES DOWN ON GAZA ADVOCACY, TARGETS ‘UNCANCELLABLE’ CELEBRITIES FOR STAYING SILENT

In one post about the visit, she wrote, "I’m still processing being outside Delaney Hall Immigration Detention Center in NJ yesterday. I can’t say enough wonderful things about the children and families whose loved ones are inside. I can’t say enough about how this cruelty is harming and traumatizing precious children who should get to just be kids. I know if you came and played cars and drew with chalk with them and laughed and sang and saw their tears you wouldn’t want what is happening to happen."

A graphic shared on her Instagram account from the account, @readlikearockstarteaching, read, "Your toddler notices race. And talking about it isn’t what teaches them racism."

In her caption, ​​Ms. Rachel wrote, "Brilliant info from @readlikearockstarteaching - please follow!"

A Dec. 4 post from Ms. Rachel read, "Just so you know, you are welcome in Ms Rachel’s classroom & I love you. People who are trans, gay, nonbinary, people who are Somali, people who are any religion – Muslim, Jewish, Christian or not religious, people who use food stamps, Democrats, Republicans, people who are undocumented, people who hate me."

MS RACHEL CLAIMS 'NO ONE NEEDS A BILLION DOLLARS,' ENDORSES DEMOCRATIC PROGRESSIVES ABDUL EL-SAYED, CORI BUSH

Descovich said that parents should be clearly informed when a children’s entertainer uses a trusted toddler-focused platform to promote political views.

"What's most important here is that parents are informed on Ms. Rachel's political ideologies because they are starting to seep into all of the work she's doing with their children," Descovich said. "So, parents need to be informed, they ultimately get to choose and direct the upbringing of their children, but they absolutely should not be manipulated or, you know, sideswiped by thinking they're putting their child in front of Mr. Rogers when they're really getting a political radical like Ms. Rachel."

Fox News Digital reached out to Ms. Rachel for comment.

item.title: Bucs provide Baker Mayfield injury update as team set to play undrafted rookie at quarterback
item.description: Baker Mayfield expects to miss a "minimum" of three weeks for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, Todd Bowles says as an MRI revealed no ligament damage.
item.content:encoded:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers can breathe a little easier on Monday.

Baker Mayfield is only expected to miss a "minimum" of three weeks after he dislocated his right thumb in the Buccaneers’ loss to the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday, head coach Todd Bowles said. Mayfield was writhing in pain on the ground after suffering the injury.

"We’ll keep him on (the active roster) right now but we’re not sure," Bowles said. "It could be, possibly, sooner. We’ll know how it goes how it’s gonna go."

Mayfield suffered the injury throwing the ball down the field as he was rolling to his right. His hand came down on Vikings linebacker Blake Cashman. The ball was intercepted and Mayfield hit the ground with the broadcast picking up his frightful screams.

An MRI didn’t reveal any ligament damage or fracture.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Mayfield agreed to a contract extension before the start of the season. The deal is worth $165 million over three years. He hadn’t missed a game before he joined the Buccaneers following stints with the Los Angeles Rams, Carolina Panthers and Cleveland Browns.

Tampa Bay’s loss to Minnesota dropped the team to 0-3. It’s the team’s worst start since 2014.

Undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels will likely be thrust into the starting quarterback role. He was 0-for-3 with an interception when he came in for Mayfield at the end of the game.

Daniels played his collegiate career at Kansas. Last year with the Jayhawks, he had 2,531 passing yards and 22 passing touchdowns to go along with 404 yards on the ground and four rushing touchdowns.

"He's going to be like every other rookie, but he's played well in the preseason. He's very bright," Bowles said of the rookie. "He's not going to be out there by himself. There'll be 22 other guys out there helping him out. So, you know, we just expect him to do his job and play at a high level as he expects from himself."

item.title: Protester storms DC party, flips off crowd as ‘USA!’ chants erupt amid Trump’s AI push
item.description: A protester crashed a Washington, D.C., data center party, shouting about water use as Trump pushes AI dominance and rapid buildout over China.
item.content:encoded:
Protesters crashed a large pro-data center party in Washington, D.C., making obscene guestures attendees and shouting about the industry's water use as President Donald Trump pushes to accelerate America's artificial intelligence and data center boom.

"Thank you for using all of our water!" and "You’re killing the world," the protester shouted as a woman interrupted the party, directing middle fingers at the crowd while chanting against the data center industry.

The "Data After Dark" party was hosted by three self-proclaimed data center "fanboys," bringing together more than 600 people to show support for data center infrastructure.

FIRST ON FOX: ‘NO KINGS’ PROTEST NETWORK BEHIND FIGHT AGAINST AI DATA CENTERS AND FLOCK CAMERAS

Party co-host and Young Voices CEO Casey Givens told Fox News Digital that one protester initially approached him asking to give a toast in support of data centers, but after he refused, she jumped onstage and attempted to grab the microphone from co-host Jonas Du.

After the protester was removed by security, the crowd responded by chanting, "USA, USA, USA."

Data centers power artificial intelligence by housing thousands of high-performance computers that store, process and analyze data, enabling AI systems to be trained and operate.

INSIDE THE FAR-LEFT'S ANTI-DATA CENTER PUSH AND WHAT EXPERTS SAY IS DRIVING IT: 'PLAYBOOK WE'VE SEEN BEFORE'

"I organized the party along with my co-hosts because the three of us were dismayed by how one side was dominating the data center conversation with hysteria instead of reason," said Givens.

"We wanted to push back by throwing a celebration of technology and benefits of data centers — locally in terms of tax revenue and economic development, and nationally in terms of innovation and the fight against China," Givens added.

The party featured themed cocktails such as "Loudoun County Iced Tea," named after the Northern Virginia county that handles more than 70% of global internet traffic across roughly 250 data centers, according to the county's website.

CHINA ‘THROWING GASOLINE ON THE FIRE’ IN AI DATA CENTERS RACE, SAY LAWMAKERS

Trump has pushed for a rapid buildout of data centers as part of his broader AI agenda, contending the U.S. must stay ahead of China in the global AI race and that resistance to the projects gives Beijing an advantage.

"If you want to go through poverty, crime and squalor, I would say don’t approve of data centers," Trump said from the Oval Office Sept. 4.

Trump boasted about American AI supremacy over China during an address to the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) in New York Tuesday, using his newly-minted term for the technology, "superintelligence."

"Every major new technology brings challenges, and superintelligence is no exception," said Trump. "Whoever wins superintelligence wins. That's the group that wins. And we're leading now over China by a lot and everyone else. And we're going to keep it that way."
